selection: Purposive public-report examples, labelled Reports A--F for readability. Names, locations, dates and URLs are omitted from the published package. None of these reports is a row in the generated matrices.

reports.title: Public investigation report A
reports.use: Direct loss comprises more than property. Component boundaries differ from our illustrative decomposition.

reports.title: Public investigation report B
reports.use: One-fatality road-freight collision loss scale; not a compensation schedule.

reports.title: Public investigation report C
reports.use: Truck/tanker collision; total loss is not a pure fatality cost.

reports.title: Public investigation report D
reports.use: External persons can be exposed in a truck collision with a crowd; totals are descriptive.

reports.title: Public investigation report E
reports.injury_definition_note: Opening paragraph says six injured, including four who subsequently died. Do not treat six as an unambiguous disjoint final injury count.
reports.use: Tanker/cargo fire and bus involvement can produce mass casualties; no reproduction of a report row.

reports.title: Public investigation report F
reports.use: Community exposure and damage to surrounding property; extreme-event example, not a population maximum.

quantitative_status: No distribution is fitted to these six reports. All mixture weights, factor rates, component coefficients and shift sizes remain explicit assumptions. Cross-year monetary amounts are not pooled as inflation-adjusted estimates.
audit_note: The original public source ledger and access URLs remain in the internal revision workspace. The published package retains only anonymized mechanism examples and the fact that retrieval checks were performed.

last_access_check.report_e: TLS transport failure during final check

anonymization: The clean ledger omits real accident names, locations, dates, publishers and URLs.
